_cody, 2026-11-16 06:49:_

Decision: The rules live in their own repo, bryantserver/project-rules, not in cody/agents or any project's README. Repos carry them as enforced settings (branch protection, required checks) plus a short CONTRIBUTING-style file that points here and adds only repo-specific notes. Decided by: Cody, 2026-11-16.

_cody, 2026-11-16 06:49:_

Decision: The upstream small-teaching mode (small chunks, Cody approving every commit and PR) does not carry over yet, maybe one day. Only the upstream craft rules do: smallest correct diff, one concern per PR, every hunk maps to the issue, regression tests proven to fail first, declared checks run, docs in the same PR. CI and the AI review are the gate. Why: Per-PR approval would stall merges while Cody is away; the craft rules are what keep diffs reviewable.

Decided by: Cody, 2026-11-16.

_cody, 2026-11-16 06:52:_

_cody, 2026-11-16 07:23:_

Technical call: Diff size limit is 400 changed lines, not counting tests, lockfiles and generated files; over it needs `Large diff: <reason>` in the PR description, judged by the AI review, rather than a warning-only check. Why: Casa's largest PR so far was 291 lines; a stated reason is cheap for a legitimate big diff, while a bare warning gets ignored. Cody asked whether it should be soft (2026-11-16); revisit if it blocks real work.

Decided by: agent, 2026-11-16.

Why: One public rulebook every contributor can read, with a clean history.

Decided by: Cody, 2026-11-16.

_cody, 2026-11-16 13:52:_

Decision: Leave the Forgejo account name as is; hiding the real name is not possible (login and past commits). Rules text says 'the maintainer'; other people's names stay out of everything public. Why: The name is already public in past commits and the login.

Decided by: Cody, 2026-11-16.

_cody, 2026-11-16 13:52:_

Technical call: Public repos get no ISSUE_READ_TOKEN: they read cross-repo issues unauthenticated only. The new repo is built private and made public only on Cody's yes, after a scan of its tree and recreated issues. Why: issue-link prints the linked issue's title in CI logs and the AI review posts from linked issue text, both public in a public repo; private issue content would leak.

Decided by: agent, 2026-11-16.

_cody, 2026-11-16 13:57:_

Decision: Coverage stays at 99% branch coverage overall and 100% on safety-critical code in every repo; project-standard's measure-first rule is replaced. Why: One strict, simple bar every repo is held to.

Decided by: Cody, 2026-11-16.

_Recreated from bryantserver/project-rules#15 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-11-16, merged 2026-11-16). Branch `refs/pull/15/head` into `main`._

Closes #14
Refs #2

Rule 8 set a 400-line limit, but nothing enforced it. New `Diff size` job: it sums added and deleted lines from `git diff --numstat base...head`, skipping test paths (same definition as Tests with code) and lockfiles, and fails over 400 unless the description has `Large diff: <reason>`. It runs main's copy of the script, so a PR cannot raise its own limit. Renames count only their edits; a rename from code into `tests/` still counts, so moving code into a test path is not a way around it. Rule 8 now says "tests and lockfiles": generated code goes through the `Large diff:` reason instead of an exclusion a PR could claim for itself.

Tests (`tests/test_diff_size.py`, 8): code counted, tests and lockfiles not; deletions counted; pure rename 0; rename into tests counted; binary 0; exactly 400 passes; 401 fails; 401 with a reason passes; an empty reason fails. Checked they fail with the rename rule or the test filter broken. CONTRIBUTING.md gets the test command.

This job does not run on this PR (main's ci.yml has no such job yet). It becomes a required check after the next PR shows it passing.

Renovate can raise `PROJECT_STANDARD` but cannot fetch the tag it then names, so every standard bump landed red and was closed as obsolete.

- `revendor-standard.sh` reads the pin, clones that tag (bounded three ways) and runs its `vendor.py`
- `vendor.py` now retires files the standard stopped shipping, and replaces by rename so a script can update itself mid-run
- `CONVENTIONS.md` corrected: the pinned Renovate image does carry python3 (verified 3.12.3 against the digest), but a script must check rather than assume

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#3 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-23, merged 2026-08-23). Branch `refs/pull/3/head` into `main`._

Consumers enumerate Renovate `fileFilters`. A shared file outside that shape is written on the update branch, dropped before the commit, and leaves a lock describing content the branch does not have.

Only this end can refuse the first such file: the consumers can check what is already in their lock, not what a future tag will add.

_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#7 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-24, merged 2026-08-25). Branch `refs/pull/7/head` into `main`._

This entry merged two decisions, and the merge produced confident wrong answers — twice in one session, from me.

**Decision 1, the bundle mode:** invisible in packaged channels, visible at runtime. macOS onefile is platform-driven (one Mach-O to codesign per frozen app, not an executable plus every `.so`; notarization acts on the `.pkg` either way, so it is not the reason). Linux onedir is **not** platform-driven and the entry now says so.

**Decision 2, the standalone download shape:** whiskerless ships a bare binary, dreame a tarball, because dreame's download must carry `dreame-fastboot` and `sunxi-fel`.

Two rationales were retired for not surviving scrutiny: that helpers require onedir (macOS ships the same helpers beside a onefile app) and that dreame pays the unpack repeatedly (it pays it twice at start, then once per human rejoin — bounded, not recurring). What remains is one real property — onefile cannot run where `TMPDIR` is `noexec` — and the honest reason to leave it alone: not churning a shipped artifact.
title: Separate the bundle mode from the download shape, and stop overclaiming the Linux mode

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#8 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-25, merged 2026-08-25). Branch `refs/pull/8/head` into `main`._

`build-bottles.sh` waits for publish.yml first tap pass; publish second pass then waits for the bottles built here. That handshake is correct. The BUDGET was not: 90 x 20s = 30 minutes, against a publish measured at 37m18s. The tap appeared 60 seconds after the loop gave up, and a release lost its bottles and the install matrix that waits on them.

Now 270 x 20s = 90 minutes. Widening is close to free: the loop breaks the moment the formula appears, so this is a FAILURE bound rather than a delay.

This applies to stable as much as to candidates - bottles.yml triggers on v*.*.* - and stable publish does more before the tap pass while a stable tag is permanent.

Both consumers gain a repo-local invariant failing under a 60-minute budget, mutation-tested against fewer iterations AND a shorter sleep.
title: Wait 90 minutes for the tap, not 30

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#10 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-28, closed 2026-08-29). Branch `refs/pull/10/head` into `main`._

Both repos now gate their tree against committed hardware addresses with the same matcher. whiskerless additionally gates serials and dreame-valetudo does not — recorded here so a future convergence pass does not read it as accidental drift.

An LR4 serial has a fixed shape and doubles as the MQTT client-id and both topic segments. A Dreame serial is [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{5,63}, so the same guard would match ordinary prose on every run, and a test that always fails is a test somebody deletes.
title: Record why only the MAC half of the privacy guard converges

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#11 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-29, merged 2026-08-29). Branch `refs/pull/11/head` into `main`._

dreame rc.41 failed its publish at "tag never appeared on GitHub": the push-mirror had errored with context deadline exceeded and Forgejo does not retry, so the job waiting for the tag timed out ten minutes later, far from the cause.

push_mirrors-sync answers 403 to the repo-scoped token the release uses, which is why the call has always been best-effort — so a retry keyed on its result would never run. What is checkable without extra scope is the OUTCOME: the GitHub mirror is public, so an unauthenticated ref lookup says whether the tag arrived.

One bounded POST, then read-only polling, three-state: arrived / definitively absent / unknown. A check that cannot answer reports unknown rather than claiming failure. Still warn-only — a release whose refs already fanned out must not be failed by a mirror.

Also: ci.yml named one test file explicitly, so tests/*.sh added later never ran. It now discovers them.
title: Confirm the tag reached the mirror instead of assuming the sync worked

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#12 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-29, merged 2026-08-29). Branch `refs/pull/12/head` into `main`._

`$?` taken directly after a `[ ]`/`[[ ]]` is the condition's status, which shellcheck flags as SC2319 and which any command inserted before the read would silently replace. Builds `rc` explicitly instead.

This is what has been failing the Shell scripts job on main, so it blocks #10 and #11.
title: test(release): build assertion status explicitly instead of reading it from a condition

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#13 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-29, merged 2026-08-29). Branch `refs/pull/13/head` into `main`._

The confirmation added in v0.1.22 checked only that GitHub answered 200 for the tag name. An rc number is derived from the source tags alone, so a name can be reused, and a ref left behind by a partial prune answers 200 while still pointing at the previous release - every job waiting on the mirror would then run against the wrong commit.

Compares the object the mirror serves with the one just pushed. The test gains that case.
title: fix(release): compare the mirrored tag object, since a reused tag name answers 200 while stale

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#14 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-08-29, merged 2026-08-29). Branch `refs/pull/14/head` into `main`._

Unauthenticated github.com allows 60 requests an hour per IP and every runner, mirror probe and CI poller shares one. Several helpers treated their token as optional, so once the budget was gone they did not fail - they answered 403, and the checks built on them stopped deciding anything while still reporting success. The republish guard did exactly that on its first real run.

Every GitHub caller now makes its token mandatory: push-tag.sh, check-mirror-ci.sh, check-rc-install-matrix.sh, reconcile-releases.sh, github-release.sh. reconcile also authenticates the asset download, which was reaching GitHub bare.

push-tag.sh asserts its token BEFORE `git push --atomic`, since discovering it afterwards would leave the tag published and the run failed - and only when a mirror is configured, so the documented no-project.env mode still pushes.

`tests/test-github-auth.sh` pins all of it, including the shapes that previously slipped through: a credential-free `auth` array that keeps its name, an auth helper whose github arm is gone, a sourced library that drops the inherited array, and the guard being moved below the push. Each has a negative control.
title: fix(release): require a credential on every GitHub call instead of degrading to unauthenticated

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#17 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-09-16, merged 2026-09-16). Branch `refs/pull/17/head` into `main`._

Observed on whiskerless run 35055059591: `brew test` bootstrapped Homebrew's Ruby harness and the macOS runner could not resolve rubygems.org. The failure landed in one of our named steps, so the step-name rule refused the retry and the run stayed red until Renovate pushed again.

The discriminator now also reads each failed job's log. A step of ours is retryable only when its closing lines, bounded to its own timestamps with boundary seconds excluded, carry an exact resolver-failure spelling AND name a host CI is known to reach. Tests pin the refusals: a log printed by another step, a resolver error the step survived, a typo'd hostname, timeouts and refusals, a missing log, and a genuine failure elsewhere in the run.

Consumers need `gh api --allow-escape-sequences .../jobs/<id>/logs` per failed job and to pass the logs directory; that lands with the pin bump in each.
title: feat(retry): also retry a step the runner's resolver failed

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#21 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-10-09, merged 2026-10-09). Branch `refs/pull/21/head` into `main`._

platformAutomerge: false, so Renovate merges an automerge PR itself once its checks are green. With platform automerge Forgejo merged immediately when main required no checks: archiver #192 (an rclone bump) merged 3 seconds after opening and broke the image build. Cody approved this change across the bryantserver and SisyphusMD repos (2026-10-09).
title: chore(renovate): automerge only after CI passes

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#27 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-10-26, merged 2026-10-26). Branch `refs/pull/27/head` into `main`._

Homebrew stopped building Intel macOS bottles in 2026-09, so both consumers drop the `sequoia` bottle leg. `update-tap.sh` now demands 3 tags. `bottle-block.py` keeps `sequoia` in `TAG_ORDER` (ordering only, not required).
title: fix(packaging): demand three bottles, not four

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#29 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-10-26, merged 2026-10-26). Branch `refs/pull/29/head` into `main`._

Every push to main makes Renovate rebase its whole backlog, and each rebased branch queued two macOS runs on the GitHub mirror (~30 per main push), most for Dockerfile digests or Forgejo workflows no Mac reads. Real verdicts waited hours behind them.

`macos-scope.sh <ref>` prints true/false. Only `refs/heads/renovate/*` can be skipped, and only when every changed path (renames split with --no-renames) is on an anchored Linux-only list. Anything undecidable runs.

Consumers gate their ci-macos.yml / formula-macos.yml jobs on it next, and let renovate/* runs cancel superseded ones.
title: feat(packaging): macos-scope.sh — let Renovate branches skip the GitHub macOS workflows when only Linux-side files change

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#30 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-10-26, merged 2026-10-26). Branch `refs/pull/30/head` into `main`._

Both consumers had their own wait-for-release.sh and they had drifted: dreame treated the tap as ready on a `bottle do` block plus a version substring, never comparing bottle sha256s to the release manifests; whiskerless hardcoded its names and had a garbled section.

This is one project-agnostic script (union of both checks), parameterised from project.env (`PROJECT_REPO_SLUG`, new `PROJECT_TAP_SLUG`) and a per-repo `asset-roles.sh` data file. `fetch()` is confined to `$FORGE` and follows no redirects. Also: release-output entries in gitignore.base, VARIANCE contribution-routing line corrected (dreame has ci-pr.yml).
title: feat(packaging): share wait-for-release.sh and release-output gitignore entries

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#31 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-10-26, merged 2026-10-26). Branch `refs/pull/31/head` into `main`._

Killing the watchdog subshell orphaned its `sleep`, which inherited stdout. Anything reading the output (a pipe, Renovate post-upgrade capture) waited the full 300 s clone deadline after the vendor was done. The watchdog now traps TERM and kills its own sleep, and its output goes to /dev/null. tests/test-revendor-watchdog.sh times it (old script: 30 s stall at a 30 s deadline; new: 0 s).
title: fix(packaging): revendor-standard.sh no longer holds its output open after finishing

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#35 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-11-13, merged 2026-11-13). Branch `refs/pull/35/head` into `main`._

GitHub cancels a macOS arm64 job it cannot place after 15 minutes ("not acquired by Runner"). It ends `cancelled`, which the triage treated as a veto, so whiskerless rc.74 and rc.75 sat red until rerun by hand. This adds that class with exact evidence (no steps, no runner, GitHub annotation), and lets it alone retry up to attempt 5.
title: fix(triage): retry a job no runner ever took

body:
_Recreated from SisyphusMD/project-standard#37 (pull request, opened by cody on 2026-11-16). Branch `ci/agit-pr-guard` into `main`._

Forgejo treats an AGit pull request (pushed to `refs/for/main`, no fork needed) as untrusted and holds its runs for approval, but its payload reports this repository as the head (`head.repo.full_name == github.repository`), so the existing fork gate let it through. When a maintainer acts on an outsider's PR (reopen), Forgejo 17 runs this branch's workflows, with secrets, against the PR's commit (services/actions/trust.go). Outside contributors are about to be able to sign in with GitHub and open AGit PRs, so the gate now also requires `github.event.pull_request.flow == 0`.

Proof (throwaway SisyphusMD/agit-guard-proof-20261116): an AGit PR's payload has `flow=1` and head repo = base repo, and the gated job was skipped (run 37485); a branch PR has `flow=0` and the gated job ran (run 37486).

Outside PRs get CI when a maintainer, after reading the diff, pushes the head to a branch here.

CONVENTIONS.md states the gate the same way, so new projects copy the full condition.

_Still open when project-standard was retired: its change is not in this repo. It lands here as a new pull request that closes this issue._
title: ci: keep AGit pull requests off the self-hosted runner (they report this repo as their head, so the fork gate let them through, and a maintainer's reopen runs this branch's workflows with secrets)
